name: Fine-Tuning for Tool Use and Agent Trajectories
question: Can a small model learn to use our tools as well as a big one?
summary: General supervised fine-tuning teaches style and format; agent fine-tuning teaches a model to act. Each example is a whole trajectory: the user request, the assistant’s tool calls with arguments, the tool results and the final reply, in the model’s own chat and tool-call template. Trajectories come from production logs or from a strong teacher model run in a sandbox, and only those verified to have succeeded are kept. Loss is computed on assistant turns only, so the model learns to call tools rather than to invent tool results. The payoff is a small model that runs your agent loop at a fraction of the cost and latency, judged on end-to-end task success, not on text similarity. LoRA mechanics are covered by Supervised Fine-Tuning; learning from rewards by RLVR.
useCases: Replacing a large model in a high-volume agent with a small one
Proprietary tools and schemas a general model keeps getting wrong
On-premise agents where a large hosted model is not allowed

steps.title: Store trajectories as chat messages
steps.text: Yatra Setu, a fictional travel-booking company, logs each booking run as messages with tool calls and tool results, plus the tool schemas, in the same template the model will be served with.

steps.title: Keep verified successes
steps.text: A sandbox checks each run’s end state: was the right train held for the right date and seats? 2,000 of 3,100 teacher trajectories pass and are kept.

steps.title: Mask everything but the assistant
steps.text: With assistant-only loss, the model learns to write tool calls and replies. It never learns to write tool outputs, which is how models start inventing results.

steps.title: Train a LoRA adapter
steps.text: Two epochs of LoRA on an 8B model take a few GPU-hours. Data generation by the teacher was the larger cost.

steps.title: Evaluate in the sandbox
steps.text: 300 held-out tasks run end to end. Score task success, valid tool calls and invented tool results, not text overlap.

steps.title: Compare with the teacher
steps.text: The base 8B model succeeds on 48% and the teacher on 78%; the tuned 8B reaches 73% at about one fifteenth of the cost per task.

practice.scenario: Yatra Setu, a fictional travel-booking company, runs a booking agent with tools to search trains, hold seats and take UPI payments. A large model completes 78% of tasks but costs about ₹6 a task; the base 8B model completes 48%. It runs the large model as a teacher in a sandbox, keeps 2,000 of 3,100 trajectories whose end states were verified, and fine-tunes the 8B model with LoRA on assistant turns only. The tuned model completes 73% of held-out tasks, invents tool results in 2% of runs, and costs about ₹0.40 a task.

industries.use: Booking agents with search, hold and payment tools
Back-office agents calling core-banking APIs on-premise
Plan-change agents with proprietary provisioning tools

practice.analogy: Training a new booking clerk by having them watch only the calls a senior clerk handled well, and practise their own lines, not the customer’s or the computer’s.

practice.note: assistant_only_loss needs a chat template that marks assistant turns; check the TRL docs for your model. The file format is one JSON object per trajectory with messages, tools and verified_success.

samples.code:
import json

kept, total = [], 0
with open("teacher_runs.jsonl", encoding="utf-8") as f:
    for line in f:
        run = json.loads(line)
        total += 1
        end = run["end_state"]
        ok = (end.get("pnr") is not None and end.get("seats") == run["task"]["seats"]
              and end.get("date") == run["task"]["date"])
        if ok and len(run["messages"]) <= 30:            # drop long, looping runs
            kept.append({"messages": run["messages"], "tools": run["tools"], "verified_success": True})

with open("trajectories.jsonl", "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
    for r in kept:
        f.write(json.dumps(r, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n")
print(f"kept {len(kept)} of {total} runs")

numericDrill.question: A task costs ₹6 with the large model and ₹0.40 with the tuned 8B. At 50,000 tasks a month, what is the monthly saving in ₹?
numericDrill.answer: (6 − 0.40) × 50,000 = 5.6 × 50,000 = ₹2,80,000 a month. The ₹42,000 data and training cost pays back in under a week.

interview.question: How would you fine-tune a small model to run an agent?
interview.answer: Collect trajectories from logs or a teacher in a sandbox, keep only runs whose end state was verified, format them in the serving chat and tool template, train LoRA with loss on assistant turns only, and evaluate end-to-end task success on held-out tasks.

interview.question: Why mask tool outputs during training?
interview.answer: If tool outputs carry loss, the model learns to write them, and at run time it may invent a result instead of calling the tool.
